contents.name: Proposition 4.3.2 (division-algebra index and divisibility clauses)
contents.reason: These stronger index/center-degree identities are retained for the downstream Schur-index page; this supplier proves orbit classification and common multiplicity.

contents.name: Corollary 4.3.3 (character independence)
contents.reason: Full nonmodular character independence has a separate character-theory home and is not used to prove the orbit classification.

contents.name: Realizability definition and Corollary 4.3.4
contents.reason: The global splitting-field realization equivalence belongs to the existing fields-of-definition theory; the examples here compute their own models.

contents.support: Finite-dimensional proof expanded from earlier basis extension, characteristic, finite-sum and induction items; avoids the defective published Maschke chain.

sources.title: Gábor Wiese, Galois Representations
sources.locator: §2.2 Definition 2.2.7 through Corollary 2.2.12, printed pp.28–30; Remark 2.4.2(ii), p.34; §2.5, pp.37–41; Exercise 14, p.70

contents.name: Definition 2.2.7 (Galois twists, decomposition group)
contents.support: Pullback by σ inverse; our definition explicitly changes the scalar structure and fixes transported-basis conventions.

contents.name: Remark 2.2.8 (twists and scalar extension)
contents.support: The printed claim that the K-vector structure stays equal conflicts with its scalar-action formula. Our additive-group formulation removes that ambiguity.

contents.name: Lemma 2.2.10 (extension of a restricted module)
contents.reason: The restriction-extension decomposition is an alternative proof route; the assigned design uses central idempotent descent and does not need this extra theorem.

contents.name: Proposition 2.2.11 (indecomposable orbit theorem)
contents.reason: The indecomposable nonsemisimple generalization uses Krull–Schmidt and is broader than this semisimple supplier; the simple case is retained below.

contents.name: Lemma 2.5.2 (character field and twist stabilizer)
contents.reason: This character-field criterion is downstream fields-of-definition material; the orbit theorem uses the algebra action, without invoking character independence.

contents.name: Lemma 2.5.3 (nonsplit characteristic-polynomial variant)
contents.reason: The nonsplit variant needs Brauer–Nesbitt and is not needed under the explicit split-algebra hypothesis of this supplier.

contents.name: Corollary 2.5.4 (isotypic extension over the character field)
contents.reason: This downstream consequence of orbit classification is reserved for the existing Schur-index page and is not imported back as a premise.

contents.name: Corollaries 2.5.5–2.5.6 (fixed field and orbit size)
contents.reason: The character-field/stabilizer identification belongs to the later fields-of-definition page; abstract orbit sizes do not need it here.

contents.name: Corollary 2.5.7 (index equals multiplicity)
contents.reason: The division-algebra index identity is a later consumer of this classification, not an earlier premise; the quaternion instance is computed directly.

contents.name: Corollary 2.5.10 (realizability and multiplicity one)
contents.support: Used as independent source backing for the obstruction; local verification supplies explicit rational matrices and a multiplicity-two model.

contents.name: Corollary 2.5.11 (splitting the endomorphism algebra)
contents.reason: This general field-of-definition test is not needed for the elementary quaternion witness and belongs to the later Schur-index theory.

contents.name: Definition 2.5.12, Corollary 2.5.13, Remark 2.5.15 (Schur index)
contents.reason: The general minimal-field-degree definition and equality require the downstream division-algebra theory; the example here only computes multiplicity two.

contents.name: Corollary 2.5.14 (finite-field and degree-two realizability bounds)
contents.reason: The local-field and finite-field realizability generalizations are outside this characteristic-zero finite-group supplier and are not required for its examples.

contents.name: Exercise 14 (Hamilton quaternion splitting)
contents.support: An exercise, not a supplied proof: all norm, splitting and multiplicity calculations are specified in the scaffold, with Q replacing R and Q(i) replacing C.
